replies:
Good — I'll run a live mock. I'll ask the first interview question now; answer as you would in the room, and I'll score it on structure, evidence and specificity, then give one concrete improvement and the next question.

Here's the first question:

"Walk me through your resume — highlight the experiences that make you a strong fit for a financial analyst role on our team."

Score: 2/10.

Short feedback (what the interviewer hears and how to fix it):
- Structure (1/3): your answer jumps to the action. Reorder to Situation → Task → Action → Result.
- Evidence (0/4): no measurable outcome. Say a number (accuracy improvement, $ impact, % variance reduction, or days saved) or, if you don't have one, state the direction and why.
- Specificity (1/3): name the tools, the inputs, constraints and your role (lead, reviewer, owner), and what "check it against comps" means (which comps, which metrics).
Rewritten answer (2–3 sentences) you can use in the interview:
"At [Company], I owned forecasting for a $[X] revenue stream that was missing by about [Y]% month-to-month (S/T). I built a three‑statement [your skill] model driven from price, volume and churn using historical cohorts and seasonality, linked it to the cash‑flow and balance sheet, and stress‑tested it with comps from [competitor names or public filings] (A). That process improved forecast accuracy to within [Z]% and cut month‑end close time by [T] days, giving leadership confidence to size a $[M] financing decision (R)."
One concrete improvement to make now:
- Replace each bracket with a real value or, if you don't have exact numbers, state the direction and why (e.g., "reduced variance vs. prior model" or "shortened close by several days").

Next question for the mock:
"Tell me about a time you found an error in a model under deadline — what did you do and what happened?"

You gave a one-line technical summary — it shows you know the core approach, but it misses everything interviewers listen for. Honest score: 2/10.

Why I scored it that way (short):
- Structure: 1 — no S/T/A/R, just the action.
- Evidence: 0 — no metrics or outcome.
- Specificity: 1 — method named, but no tools, inputs, constraints or role.

What that actually signals to interviewers:
- You know how to build a model, but you don't own outcomes or communicate impact.
- You may be technical but not business‑oriented: no results or stakeholder framing.
- You give senior interviewers nothing to evaluate beyond jargon.
One concrete, immediate fix:
- Turn that one line into 3 sentences: 1) one-sentence situation and task (what you were asked to do and why), 2) two specific actions (tools, inputs, what "comps" were), 3) one measurable result or, if you don't have numbers, the qualitative impact and whom it affected.

If you want, I’ll rewrite your exact answer into that 3-sentence STAR form using placeholders you can fill, or you can paste a real resume bullet and I’ll tailor it to your experience. Which do you want?

replies:
You don't have any Lincoln International application or interview recorded on file yet. The one step that starts that record is: paste the interview invite or confirm the role, date/time and interviewers so I can save it and build a tailored prep plan.

Prep now for a final-round analyst interview at Lincoln International — here’s a focused plan, likely question set, and how to answer.
What they want in an analyst (how to show it)
- Technical rigor: accurate accounting, modeling basics, and comfort with valuations (comps, precedent, DCF). Show method, not guesses. If you don’t know a number, show the steps you’d take.
- Commercial judgment: understanding deal rationale and value drivers. Tie numbers to business sense.
- Drive and fit: reliability, attention to detail, long hours. Use concrete examples of when you caught an error, learned fast, or owned a deliverable.
- Teamwork and communication: clear, concise updates and ability to ask the right question, not all questions.
10-point prep checklist (do these in order)
1) Send me (paste) the interview invite or list the interviewers, format and time so I record it. (one step)
2) Re-read the job posting and listing of skills — note any words I should mirror in answers. If you paste it, I’ll extract the keywords.
3) Review one live model: refresh three things — how to build a simple three-statement link, how to run a DCF (WACC, unlevered FCF, terminal value by exit multiple and Gordon), and how to set up a basic LBO (purchase price, debt schedule, equity IRR). Practice aloud for 8–10 minutes.
4) Prepare 5 crisp deal stories from your experience (buy-side, sell-side, valuation, modeling, due diligence). Each = situation, your action (what you did, tools used), outcome with a metric or concrete result, and one lesson. I can rewrite them into STAR answers.
5) Prepare 3 behavioral answers for fit: "Why Lincoln?" "Tell me about a time you missed something" "Describe a high-pressure deadline." Keep them 2–3 short sentences plus one result.
6) Mock technical Q&A: practice common interview problems (see questions below). Time answers: 60–120s for technical, 90–180s for deal stories.
7) Prepare questions to ask them (3–5): a mix of deal pipeline, team structure, training path, and a thoughtful business question about their sector focus.
8) Resume walkthrough: be ready to speak through any line on your CV in 60–90s, with a clear impact metric.
9) Logistics: plan a quiet room, copy of your resume, a notepad, and calculator or spreadsheet open. For video: camera at eye level, solid lighting, professional background.
10) One-hour before: quick mental warm-up — 5 minutes of mock answers, 5 minutes of breathing, then turn off notifications.
Most likely final-round question list (practice these)
Technical / Modeling
- Walk me through a DCF. Where do you start and what are the main drivers?
- How do you calculate WACC? What inputs move it most?
- Explain how a simple LBO works and what determines IRR.
- Given EBITDA, cash, debt and share count, walk me to Equity Value and EPS (briefly).
- How do you value a company that has negative cash flow?
Deal / Commercial
- Tell me about a deal you worked on from start to finish. What was your role?
- Pick a company in [sector you’ve worked on or Lincoln’s focus] — what are the key value drivers and risks?
- How would you pitch this company to a potential buyer? (I’ll give a one-minute answer; practice an executive summary.)

Behavioral / Fit
- Why Lincoln International? Why now?
- Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate and how you handled it.
- Describe a time you made a mistake — what happened and what did you change?
- Where do you see yourself in 3–5 years?
Questions to ask them (examples to adapt)
- What type of transactions is the team focused on right now?
- How is deal work divided between analysts and associates here?
- What are the most important skills you want a new analyst to show in the first six months?
- How does Lincoln support training and technical development for junior people?

How I’ll score your practice answers (and rewrite them)
- Structure: clear beginning (context), middle (your action), end (result/lesson).
- Evidence: one concrete metric or specific detail.
- Specificity: names, tools, exact role words whenever possible.
Send me one thing now and I’ll act on it
- Paste the interview invite (time, format, interviewer names) so I save it and create a tailored brief and question list for the actual interviewers. Or paste one answer (a deal story or "Why Lincoln?") and I’ll score and rewrite it.

Saved: nothing yet for Lincoln International. Is that right?

Here is exactly what I will prepare for that first posting, field by field, and what I will need from you for each field. I assume a standard online application with a resume upload, sometimes a cover letter and a few short fields; I will follow the posting if it asks for extra items (portfolio, salary, visa status, references).
1) Employer name and job title
- What I will place: the exact company and title text copied from the posting.
- What I need: nothing — I copy it from the posting you give me.

2) Location / work type
- What I will place: the location line exactly as posted (city, state, or “Remote”; or hybrid/on-site wording).
- What I need: tell me if you must restrict this (e.g., must be fully remote); otherwise I use the posting text.
3) Resume (PDF upload)
- What I will place: a tailored PDF resume that leads with your confirmed facts that match the posting’s top skills and phrases.
- What I need from you now: paste your resume here or confirm which saved resume name and the exact name and email to print at its header. If you paste your resume I will read it and suggest two specific improvements before making the PDF.
4) Cover letter / optional note (if the posting requests or you want one)
- What I will place: a 250–450 word targeted cover letter draft that ties your top relevant achievements to the posting’s requirements and why you want the role.
- What I need: any missing specifics I can’t infer (hiring manager name, one concrete metric you want cited). If you prefer no cover letter, say so — I default to including one only if the posting asks or you say “include it.”
5) Contact info fields (phone, email, LinkedIn)
- What I will place: the exact phone and email string you provide; LinkedIn only if you give a link.
- What I need: the phone number and the exact email you want on the application (type them here).

6) Work authorization / visa status
- What I will place: the exact status you type in; I will not guess or default beyond “available to work in [country]” if you write that.
- What I need: your work-authorization wording if the posting requests it.
7) Earliest start date / availability
- What I will place: the date or phrase you give (I will default to “Available immediately” only if you don’t specify).
- What I need: a date or “available immediately” / “available in X weeks.”

8) Salary expectation (if asked)
- What I need: exact wording or leave it blank and I will omit it.

9) Screening questions / short-answer essays
- What I will place: concise, tailored answers written as one situation → action → result, matching the posting’s skill language.
- What I need: any specific examples or numbers you want included; otherwise I’ll draft using facts from your resume when you paste it.
10) Attachments beyond resume (portfolio, code, certificates, transcripts)
- What I will place: only links or files you provide and name.
- What I need: the files or URLs you want attached.

11) References (if requested)
- What I will place: left blank unless you provide names and contact info to include.
- What I need: the names, relationships and contact info for any references you want listed.
12) Checkbox / boolean fields (willing to relocate, travel, contract type)
- What I will place: set according to your standing instruction or the posting; otherwise I will leave ambiguous or blank for you to confirm.
- What I need: any standing constraints to enforce (e.g., “no staffing agencies,” “no relocation”).

13) Optional message to recruiter / application note
- What I will place: a single short sentence (≤120 words) summarizing fit — one concrete achievement and one line why you want the role/company.
- What I need: your preferred sign-off (name, phone) and any line you insist on omitting.
14) ATS keywords and tailoring notes (internal)
- What I will prepare for you to review: the posting’s top skill words I matched to lines on your resume, plus two weaknesses/gaps and suggested fixes.
- What I need: nothing — this is for your review.

15) Final verification checklist (shown to you before any submission)
- What I will require you to confirm in the application card: resume file selected, cover letter selected (yes/no), email and phone correct, required screening answers completed, and your consent to submit.
- What I need: your approval in the browser extension; nothing is sent without that click.
What I will not do or add
- I will not invent phone, email, references, visa info or start dates — I use exactly what you give.
- I will not submit the application without your explicit approval in the extension.
- I will not attach files you haven’t provided.

Next step: paste the job link or the posting title + company you want me to prepare, and paste (or confirm you will paste) the resume header name and email to use. One question: do you want a tailored cover letter included by default, or only resume + screening answers?
